subject: Biology
description: Digestive enzymes, endocrine glands, common hormones

questions.explanation: Almost all enzymes are proteins — a small number (ribozymes) are made of RNA. They act as biological catalysts, speeding up specific chemical reactions without being consumed. Enzyme names usually end in '-ase' (amylase, protease, lipase). Vitamins often act as coenzymes, helping enzymes but not being the enzyme themselves.

questions.stem: Which hormone regulates the level of glucose (sugar) in the human blood?
questions.explanation: Insulin — secreted by beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas — lowers blood sugar by promoting glucose uptake into cells. Its opposite is glucagon (from alpha cells), which raises blood sugar. Type 1 diabetes is caused by inadequate insulin production; Type 2 by insulin resistance. Thyroxine regulates metabolism; adrenaline — stress response; oxytocin — uterine contraction and lactation.

questions.stem: The 'master gland' of the human endocrine system, which controls many other glands, is the:
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland (size of a pea, at the base of the brain) secretes several 'tropic' hormones that regulate other endocrine glands — TSH (thyroid), ACTH (adrenal cortex), FSH & LH (gonads), GH (growth), prolactin (milk), ADH and oxytocin (via posterior pituitary). The pituitary itself takes orders from the hypothalamus, so some texts call the hypothalamus the real master.

questions.stem: Goitre — enlargement of the thyroid gland — is most often caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Iodine is essential for the thyroid to make thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). Iodine deficiency causes the gland to swell (goitre) and can cause cretinism in children and hypothyroidism in adults. India mandated universal salt iodisation from 1984 to tackle this. Iron deficiency causes anaemia; calcium deficiency causes rickets / osteoporosis; zinc deficiency causes growth retardation.

questions.stem: Adrenaline — the 'fight or flight' hormone — is secreted by which gland?
questions.explanation: The adrenal medulla (inner core of the adrenal gland, one atop each kidney) secretes adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline — triggers increased heart rate, dilated pupils, muscle readiness, glucose release. The outer adrenal cortex secretes corticosteroids (cortisol — long-term stress, aldosterone — salt / water balance, sex steroids).

questions.stem: Match the enzyme with its primary site of action. A. Salivary amylase. B. Pepsin. C. Trypsin. D. Lipase (pancreatic). List-II: 1. Mouth, 2. Stomach, 3. Small intestine, 4. Small intestine (fats).
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) — mouth — breaks starch to maltose. Pepsin — stomach (acidic) — protein to peptides. Trypsin — small intestine (from pancreas, works in alkaline duodenum) — peptides to smaller peptides. Pancreatic lipase — small intestine — triglycerides to fatty acids + glycerol. Bile from the liver emulsifies fats before lipase acts.

questions.stem: Which hormone controls the body's overall rate of metabolism?
questions.explanation: Thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) — secreted by the thyroid gland — control the basal metabolic rate, body heat production, growth and brain development in children. Hypothyroidism causes weight gain and sluggishness; hyperthyroidism causes weight loss, heat intolerance and tremors (Graves' disease). Insulin controls glucose; oxytocin — labour and milk release; testosterone — male secondary characteristics.
